payload.text: The steward does not blink. He lowers the tray slowly. The wine cups stay full. He steps back into the shadow of a marble pillar. The room feels suddenly colder. You notice the other guests stop talking. They turn their heads toward you in unison. Their eyes are flat. They do not breathe. A heavy silence falls over the foyer. Three hundred pairs of eyes lock onto your group. The crystal chandeliers dim. The hum in the floor grows louder. It sounds like grinding stone. The steward raises a hand. Wood splinters.

payload.text: The iron-bound doors swing inward. Cold air hits your faces. The hall stretches long and dark above you. Tapestles hang heavy on the stone walls. They show no figures. Only grey shapes that shift when you look away. Hundreds of guests fill the room. They wear masks. Their voices sound like dry leaves rubbing together. You stand near the central fountain. The water moves in reverse. Chadwick, Leena, Vigil, Sodacan Bob, you feel the same pull. The air tastes like copper and old ash. A man in a velvet coat approaches you. He carries a silver tray. He holds out a glass. His eyes do not blink.

payload.speaker: tuber_0
payload.text: The velvet man lowers the tray. He does not blink. He turns to Leena and offers the glass. She takes it. Her fingers brush the rim. Frost blooms on her knuckles. Vigil steps to the left wall. His hand finds a seam in the stone. It is warm. Sodacan Bob watches the fountain. The water climbs the basin. It hangs there like a glass sphere. You all look at each other. The masks tilt. Three hundred heads turn toward the doorway behind you. The copper taste sharpens. A low thrum vibrates through the floorboards. Glass cracks somewhere in the crowd. The velvet man drops the silver tray. It hits the stone. The sound stops.
